# Release Notes {.unnumbered}

This course site is a living product. It gets better during the semester, and every meaningful update ships as a numbered release so you can see exactly what changed and when. The current version is shown in the footer of every page.

New entries appear at the top.

## v2.0.0 (2026-09-08)

The whole course is rebuilt around six builder skills, two weeks each. New chapters on how AI models work and how to put one inside your product. Quizzes are replaced by two testing center exams.

- **The book is now organized around the six Builder axes.** Agentic Workflow, Discovery, Design, Application Architecture, AI Systems, and Launch and Learn, two weeks each across the semester. Every chapter, every drill, and both exams line up with one of the six, so when your baseline chart says an axis is weak you know exactly where to go. You will rate yourself on all six in week 1 and again in week 13 and see how the shape changed.
- **The order changed on purpose.** Agentic Workflow comes first, so you ship something in week one that you do not fully understand, and Application Architecture comes in week seven, where you find out what you shipped. Every chapter has been renumbered to match the order you read them in.
- **New chapter, How Models Work.** What a large language model actually does when it turns your prompt into text: supervised learning, neural networks, tokens, context windows, and prompting. If you have been treating the model as magic, this is where that stops.
- **New chapter, Models in Your Product.** Calling Claude from your own app: where the call lives and why your API key never goes in the browser, getting structured data back instead of prose you have to parse, streaming, what each call costs and how to price it before you ship, the ways model calls fail without raising an error, and how to build an eval so you know whether a change actually helped.
- **New chapter, Anatomy of an Application.** Frontend, backend, database, and API, what each layer does and how they fit together, plus the tech stacks and languages this course uses and how to choose one for yourself.
- **New chapter, Interface and Flow.** Frontend fundamentals, React, forms and state, responsive layout, and the platform decision between web, PWA, and native, all in one place.
- **Quizzes are replaced by two exams.** Instead of ten in-class quizzes there is a **midterm** (Oct 20 to 26, covering the first six classes) and a **final** (Dec 14 to 17, cumulative). Both are in the testing center, on your own schedule within the window, closed book and proctored. Each is worth 5% of your grade, the same 50 points the quizzes were worth, so nothing else about grading changed. The final has ten questions per axis, so your score comes back as a six-sided profile you can compare against your own self assessment.
- **Why the exams are closed book.** Nearly everything else you submit this semester is built with AI. These two sittings are the one place your own understanding is measured on its own. They are also deliberately low stakes: at 5% each, one rough morning is worth about two percent of your grade.
- **Updated learning outcomes.** There are now five instead of four. The new one is about using AI coding agents well, including judgment about when to trust, verify, or override the tool, which is the most distinctive thing this course teaches and was not previously stated as an outcome.
- **A clearer syllabus.** The course description now describes this course rather than the version taught under the old number, and names the real tools you will use. Required Materials leads with Claude Pro at $20 per month rather than requiring Max up front. The late work policy now covers testing center windows.
- **Fixes and polish.** Growth and onboarding material moved out of the tech debt chapter into Going to Market where it belongs. Every chapter now opens with Why This Matters and closes with Key Concepts. Dates on the syllabus corrected to the Fall term.

## v1.4.0 (2026-09-08)

A new Computer Setup chapter, a new Builder Resources page, and updated office hours.

- **New chapter, Computer Setup.** Everything to get your machine ready before the first build session, in one checklist you can work through start to finish. It also explains which Claude plan to buy: **Claude Pro at $20 per month is enough to start**, and you upgrade to Claude Max at $100 per month only once you start hitting usage limits. The chapter links the Rollins Center Validation Grant, which reimburses up to $500 for customer discovery work and can offset the cost.
- **New page, Builder Resources.** The books, docs, courses, and tools behind each of the builder axes: Discovery, Design, Application Architecture, AI Systems, Agentic Workflow, and Launch and Learn. Start-here items are called out on every axis so you know what to read first.
- **Thought Leaders now includes who to follow.** The page carries the product management voices as before, plus the accounts worth following while you build and the ones worth following to understand where the field is heading. Duplicates were removed so each person appears once.
- **Office hours updated.** Wednesdays 1:30 to 3:30 PM and Fridays 3:00 to 3:30 PM, in 587 TNRB. Wednesday 3:00 to 3:30 PM and all of Friday are by phone.
- **Fixes and polish.** Clearer wording in the schedule and in the opening chapters.

## v1.3.2 (2026-07-20)

Book citations now link to Google Books.

- **Every book in the reference lists and the Works Cited page now links to its Google Books page,** where you can preview it, buy it, or find it in a library. Each link was checked to open the correct English edition. The one book that previously had no link now has one, so every source in the book is clickable.

## v1.3.1 (2026-07-20)

Every reference in the book is now a clickable link, plus three more cited sources in the economics appendix.

- **Clickable citations.** Every entry in the reference lists and the Works Cited page now links straight to the source: the book's page in an open library catalog, the publisher's article page, or a permanent archive. One out-of-print book has no free record and stays as text.
- **The Logic of Value appendix** now cites Marshall, Schumpeter, and Stewart for the economics it builds on (producer surplus, creative destruction, and economic value added).

## v1.3.0 (2026-07-20)

Every borrowed idea in the book is now cited to a real source, plus a new appendix on the economics behind strategy and a clearer opening to the AIRE loop.

- **Citations across the whole book.** Each chapter now credits the books and papers behind its ideas, with a linked reference list at the foot of the chapter and a new **Works Cited** page collecting the full bibliography (67 sources). Every entry was checked against an authoritative catalog.
- **New appendix, The Logic of Value.** Derives the economics under the value stick, how producer surplus, profit, and return above the cost of capital are one idea seen at different depths, with diagrams.
- **Product Strategy:** a new section on creating value versus capturing it, with a value stick diagram showing where your margin sits between willingness to pay and willingness to sell.
- **Chapter 1:** the AIRE loop is now framed as four plain questions (what do you want, what is true, what's the best option, what happened), opening with the Cheshire Cat as President Monson retold it.
- **Fixes and polish:** embedded tweets now show author handles correctly.

## v1.2.0 (2026-07-20)

A large release: a new Product Strategy chapter, the course reorganized around the AIRE loop, two new reference pages, and the schedule and assessments brought in line with the new structure.

- **New chapter, Product Strategy** (in the Aim part): what game you are playing, where to play and how to win, moats, and the DHM test for a strong strategy.
- **The course is now organized into five parts around the AIRE loop:** Foundations, Aim, Discover, Build, Grow, and a References section. Product Morality now sits in Aim (what is worth building), and Platform Strategy moves into Build.
- **Chapter 1 adds a table** showing how the AIRE loop (Aim, Inform, Reason, Enact) maps to the parts of the course.
- **Two new reference pages:** The Canon, which credits the sources behind each major principle and flags what has changed in the AI era, and a Thought Leaders page.
- **Attribution pass across the course:** principles are now credited to their sources, with new frameworks from Jeff Dyer added to Problems Worth Solving, Building Your MVP, Go-to-Market, and Storytelling.
- **Schedule:** the weekly practice table is rebuilt around the new parts. Product Strategy gets its own practice, and the readings and quiz schedule is updated. There are still ten quizzes; three weeks now pair two shorter chapters under one quiz.
- **Assessments:** the quiz-to-chapter mapping matches the new chapters, and all sprint, peer, final, and survey dates are corrected to the Fall 2026 calendar.

## v1.1.2 (2026-07-18)

New discovery and MVP tools, adapted with credit from Nile Hatch's *Expeditionary Innovation*.

- **Problems Worth Solving:** a "diverge before you converge" section on generating many candidate problems before narrowing.
- **Problem Discovery:** the five kinds of pain (physical, functional, financial, emotional, social) as a probing checklist, and a "how many interviews is enough?" note on interviewing to saturation.
- **Validating Opportunities:** the Access Test (can you actually reach these customers?) and a "harden your evidence" note on willingness-to-pay, the Ouch Factor, and false positives.
- **Building Your MVP:** the $100 Test for feature prioritization, and how to test demand before building (smoke test and Wizard of Oz).

## v1.1.1 (2026-07-18)

Small additions to the discovery and storytelling material.

- **Chapter 3** now has a "thinking in probabilities" note: hold beliefs about your customer as probabilities and seek evidence that would look different if you were wrong, which is why the Mom Test works.
- **A rider-and-elephant illustration** was added to the Storytelling chapter and to Product Morality, to picture the two-part mind the analogy describes.

## v1.1.0 (2026-07-18)

A large content release: a new chapter, a framework that ties the whole course together, and expanded discovery, storytelling, and grading material.

- **New chapter, Product Morality** (in Grow the Business): how to aim a product well, moral foundations, a reflection test for habit-forming products, and Aristotle's golden mean with a virtue table.
- **Chapter 1 now opens with "The Loop: How This Course Works":** the AIRE loop the course runs on (Aim, Inform, Reason, Enact), why the decision factors multiply, and how each class runs as a practice.
- **Chapter 3 now opens with "Discovery Is Truth-Seeking":** a belief-and-truth map with a new diagram, the six ways of knowing and why you triangulate, and how much evidence is enough before you commit.
- **Storytelling and the Final Demo is now a full chapter:** building a story database, techniques that make a story land, and a three-part structure for the final video.
- **New Playbook page, "Why This Class Works This Way,"** explaining the course design, including why the class is graded on decisions and learning rather than outcomes.
- **Truth-seeking callbacks** added to Validating Opportunities, Testing with Users, and Measuring What Matters.
- **Schedule:** scrimmages (Practices 11 and 12) are now described; Wednesday office hours; updated TA and course-number information.
- **Navigation reorganized** into solo-builder phases: Foundations, Discover, Build, Grow, Demo, Playbook.
- **Overview and Syllabus:** refreshed grading summary, cross-listed course numbers, and AI-tool requirements updated to the Claude Max plan.
- Fixes and polish: resources updated, version chip restyled.

The course site is now versioned. From here on, every published update to the schedule, assignments, or course content will be listed on this page with a version number and date.
